newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Davids sees 20 pct eps growth 96/97.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Davids sees 20 pct eps growth 96/97.

text.p: Grocery wholesaler and retailer Davids Ltd said on Tuesday it expected to improve its earnings per share by 20 percent in the year to June 30, 1997.

"We are confident we can maintain the percentage to turnover (ratio). If our sales are up by 20 percent, we expect profit to be up 20 percent," Davids joint managing director John Patten told reporters after a media briefing.
Earlier Patten told a function that Davids expected its incremental sales would increase by 20 percent to A$8.02 billion in the 1996/97 year.
Incremental sales includes sales within the group.
Davids earlier said that its statutory sales rose to A$3.92 billion from A$3.23 billion a year earlier.

Patten said Davids was confident of achieving 20 percent earnings growth despite higher goodwill amortisation the company would incur in 1996/97 after its acquisition of grocery wholesaler QIW Ltd and its subsidiary Composite Buyers Ltd.

Patten said although Davids was confident of maintaining its sales growth, it was not confident of maintaining market share in its retail business against retail giants Coles Myer Ltd and Woolworths Ltd.
"The real growth from the company will come from our food service business and our liquor distribution business," he said.
Earlier, Davids' chairman and founder, John David, said the company was rationalising its property portfolio and would about A$55 million worth of property on the market during 1996/97.

David said the company was also looking to sell its security services business and its Adelaide-based clothing business which it had inherited through its acquisition of Independent Holdings Ltd, which it acquired in 1994.
At 3.40 p.m. (0540 GMT), Davids shares were four cents firmer at A$1.73.
